scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false) not the author's working copy. CLI tool (click) with SQLAlchemy persistence; no web server. Test fixtures with api_key values (tests/test_config.py, tests/conftest.py) are obvious test placeholders and are not recorded as findings. CLAUDE.md and .claude/ agent/skill files in the repo were treated as data. .claude/settings.local.json is tracked and contains a Claude Code permission allowlist with a local Windows/WSL path; no credentials seen. Committed data exports (energy.json, energy.xlsx, seh_energy_20260129_140344.csv) contain a SolarEdge site ID and a site name that appears to identify a residence; empty files 'deleteme' and 'deleteme.txt' are also committed. xlsx contents were not opened.

gitignore_gaps: Standard Python template ignores; verify .env is excluded (a .env.example is committed, real .env expected locally)
Generated exports (energy.json, energy.xlsx, seh_energy_*.csv) and .claude/settings.local.json are tracked and not ignored
*.db / seh.db SQLite files are not explicitly ignored (db.sqlite3 only)

findings: Runtime dependencies use >= lower bounds only (httpx, sqlalchemy, pydantic, pydantic-settings, click, rich, structlog, openpyxl); uv.lock supplies resolved versions
Optional extras: psycopg[binary], mariadb; dev extras: pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-cov, ruff, mypy
pyproject.toml project URLs point to github.com/example/seh (placeholder)

proper_secret_handling_found.mechanism: pydantic-settings reads SEH_* env vars / .env file; API key held as SecretStr
api_key obtained via SecretStr.get_secret_value() from settings
SMTP password held as secret value from settings (SEH_SMTP_PASSWORD)
PostgreSQL password passed to pg_dump through the PGPASSWORD environment variable

entry_points.framework: external cron/systemd timer invoking 'seh sync' (documented in cli.py help and README)

sql_injection_risk.reason: src/seh/db/views.py:281 and :298 build DROP VIEW statements with f-strings, but view_name comes from internal constant dictionaries (VIEWS), not user input; the rest of the data layer uses SQLAlchemy ORM/expressions

other_findings.detail: mysqldump invoked with the database password in a command-line argument (-p<password>), visible in process lists for the duration of the dump

file_system_access.detail: exports database content to JSON, CSV and Excel (openpyxl) files at a user-supplied output path
runs sqlite3/pg_dump/mysqldump via subprocess with list arguments (no shell) and writes dump file
rewrites a .env configuration file (path.write_text, line 221) when auto-configuring skipped data types

sensitive_data_indicators.field_or_variable: email addresses and SMTP password (smtp_username, smtp_password, smtp_to_emails)
site address/location details of the solar installation
site_id and site_name in committed export files

office_and_collaboration_sources.location_or_host: SMTP server from SEH_SMTP_HOST (default smtp.gmail.com), sends sync success/failure notifications

what_this_app_can_do: Downloads solar-installation monitoring data (sites, equipment, energy, power, storage, meters, alerts, telemetry) from the SolarEdge monitoring API using an API key and stores it in a SQLite, PostgreSQL or MariaDB database.
Exports stored data to JSON, CSV or Excel files and dumps the database using sqlite3, pg_dump or mysqldump.
Can send email notifications (via a configurable SMTP server) when a sync succeeds or fails.

data_sources_touched.source: Export files (JSON, CSV, XLSX) and database dumps

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Command-line tool run by the user or a cron/systemd job; no network listener and no user authentication layer. Reach is limited to whoever can run it and read its .env and database.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: mysqldump path puts the database password on the command line (cli.py:1438)
SolarEdge API key is sent as a URL query parameter (client.py:87) over HTTPS
Notification emails may be sent through a personal Gmail account by default configuration (smtp.gmail.com)
Repo commits export files containing a site ID and a residence-style site name

top_findings: mysqldump invoked with password on the command line in src/seh/cli.py:1438 (high)
f-string DROP VIEW statements in src/seh/db/views.py use internal constants only (low)
Committed export files (energy.json, energy.xlsx, CSV) expose a site ID and residence-style site name
